claims.text: For the authentic founders who come from the field they build for, the brand is the founder and their authenticity is the proof, so it needs a medium that keeps it.
claims.quote: For them, the brand is the founder: their authenticity is the proof.

claims.text: A site written from voice memos keeps a founder's history with dates, and because every claim is checked before publication it is a record others can trust.
claims.quote: A site written from voice memos keeps it, with dates, and because every claim is checked before it is published, it is a record that others can trust.

claims.text: Building one teaches what a pure client-side site is: static files on a host, code in the reader's browser, and no server holding anyone's data.
claims.quote: Building one teaches what a pure client-side site is: static files on a host, code that runs in the reader's browser, and no server that holds anyone's data.

claims.text: GitHub Pages is free with one condition that matters: on GitHub Free the repository must be public.
claims.quote: the repository must be public

claims.text: Published GitHub Pages sites may be no larger than 1 GB, with a soft bandwidth limit of 100 GB per month.
claims.quote: Published GitHub Pages sites may be no larger than 1 GB

claims.text: Claude cloud sessions are available on Pro, Max and Team plans, run from the browser or the Claude app on a phone, and reach repositories through the Claude GitHub App.
claims.quote: run from the browser at claude.ai/code or from the Code tab of the Claude app on a phone

claims.text: The owner records with Otter; the order things were said in and the words reached for are the raw material for the founder's voice.
claims.quote: I use Otter; the order you said things in, and the words you reached for, are the raw material for your voice.

claims.text: A Stripe Payment Link takes the top-up; the site never sees card details.
claims.quote: The top-up page sends the reader to it; your site never sees card details.

claims.text: The recipe is eight steps, with a GitHub Actions workflow that validates, tags and deploys, where the rule that matters is that a failed check stops the release.
claims.quote: The rule that matters is that a failed check stops the release.

claims.text: A correction is a new version of the article with its diff, not a note about the old one, and every release gets a version and a one-line note.
claims.quote: a correction is a new version of the article, with its diff, not a note about the old one

claims.text: The house rules are one file at the root, CLAUDE.md, read at the start of every session, holding the voice, the verification rules and the release steps, growing by a line with every correction.
claims.quote: This is where your voice, your verification rules and your release steps live, and it grows by one line every time you correct the agent.

claims.text: api.newsroom.sgit.ai is a client-side API: versioned files a site loads and pins, running in the reader's browser with no server.
claims.quote: It is a client-side API: versioned files a site loads and pins

claims.text: The meter's defaults are £5 of credit to begin, 5p an article and 10p when new, with top-ups through a Stripe Payment Link the publisher owns.
claims.quote: the defaults are "£5 of credit to begin", 5p an article and 10p when new

claims.text: The meter is an honesty box, not a paywall: it never blocks a page, and because the balance is in the reader's browser a reader can change it.
claims.quote: It is an honesty box, not a paywall: it never blocks a page, and because the balance is in the reader's browser, a reader can change it.

claims.text: GitHub says Pages is not for running an online business; a writing site with an optional meter is primarily writing, and if it becomes a shop it should move.
claims.quote: A writing site with an optional meter is primarily writing; if yours becomes primarily a shop, move it to a host that allows that.

claims.text: The next step is to write the house rules as an Agent Behaviour Policy: a versioned file saying what the agent is given, what it is for and what it must not do, each rule marked by what keeps it.
claims.quote: a versioned file that says what the agent is given, what it is for, and what it must not do, with each rule marked by what keeps it

claims.text: An agent that publishes needs real privileges: it can push to the repository, which means it can publish anything to the site.
claims.quote: it can push to your repository, which means it can publish anything to your site

claims.text: A behaviour policy is not only a security control; it goes down to the business logic, how many posts a day, the tone, no Sunday publishing.
claims.quote: A behaviour policy is not only a security control; it goes all the way down to how you want the work done.

claims.text: Split the work across a writer, an editor and a publisher with separate grants, so the agent that writes cannot publish and the one that publishes cannot invent.
claims.quote: so the agent that writes cannot publish on its own, and the one that publishes cannot invent

claims.text: A policy enforced by the prompt keeps the rules in view but it is still the agent keeping them; a hook blocks the action whatever the agent intended.
claims.quote: That keeps the rules in view, but it is still the agent keeping them.

claims.text: This site's own writing session runs under a policy of eleven rules, re-read after every summary, reporting its status every few answers; more than half of its rules could move to hooks.
claims.quote: under a policy of eleven rules that is re-read after every summary and reports its status every few answers

claims.text: A more advanced setup keeps a private sgit vault beside the public repository for drafts, transcripts, data, client notes, voice guidance and the agent's working files.
claims.quote: The repository holds what is published. Beside it, an sgit vault holds the rest

claims.text: The agent clones the vault with a key given through the environment, never in a file in the repository, and only the publisher copies approved text to the public repository, so nothing private touches the public history.
claims.quote: Nothing private ever touches the public history.

claims.text: On this site, in three days, 54 messages from the owner, ten of them voice memos, became 40 releases, each with figures, sources and a section on what it does not claim.
claims.quote: in three days, 54 messages from me, ten of them voice memos, became 40 releases

value.unit: releases from 54 messages in three days

claims.text: Ask the agent to interview you when a story is thin, as a journalist challenging every answer; and let the record build on itself, every article linking to the ones before.
claims.quote: Ask the agent to interview you when a story is thin

claims.text: The writing pipeline is not a kit yet; the site's generator and release steps are published as a pattern and the brief has the agent build a smaller one.
claims.quote: The writing pipeline is not a kit yet.

claims.text: The meter trusts the reader: balances can be edited and the return page does not verify a payment, both by design.
claims.quote: Balances can be edited, and the return page does not verify a payment, both by design.

claims.text: Costs vary: GitHub Pages is free within its limits; a Claude plan, a domain and Stripe's fees are not.
claims.quote: GitHub Pages is free within its limits; a Claude plan, a domain and Stripe's fees are not.

claims.text: A public repository is public; on a free plan Pages needs it, and nothing confidential belongs in it.
claims.quote: On a free plan, Pages needs it; nothing confidential belongs in it.

claims.text: A rule in a prompt is a hope; only the rules a hook or CI keeps are enforced, so mark which is which.
claims.quote: Only the rules a hook or CI keeps are enforced; mark which is which.

claims.text: The article was updated on 15 October to add the behaviour policy and the private vault.
claims.quote: Added the behaviour policy and the private vault.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 15 October 2026, written by the site's agent in the voice of the site, with the recipe being the site's own and the sources read that day.
claims.quote: A voice memo of mine on 15 October 2026, written by this site's agent in the voice of this site
